questions.stem: At Fernway, dashboards mostly query the last 30 days of readings. Which eventhouse policy keeps that data in fast storage?

options.text: A caching policy with a 30-day hot cache period

questions.explanation: The caching policy decides how much recent data is kept in hot cache for fast queries. Retention decides how long data is kept at all.

questions.stem: Readings older than two years are never needed. Which policy removes them automatically?

options.text: A retention policy with a two-year soft delete period

questions.explanation: A retention policy removes data older than its period.

questions.stem: Dashboards repeatedly run the same heavy aggregation over an eventhouse table. What reduces the cost of those queries?

options.text: A materialized view that keeps the aggregation up to date

questions.explanation: Materialized views precompute aggregations as data arrives, so queries read a small result.

questions.stem: An eventhouse query filters on a time range. What helps it read the least data?

options.text: Filter on the datetime column early in the query, so only the relevant data is scanned

questions.explanation: Kusto indexes datetime columns efficiently. A time filter applied right after the table reference lets it skip whole data shards. Don't convert the timestamp or use contains on it.
